message:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

I hope you’re doing well. Below is a concise overview.

In August 2023, Edwin Mason and John O’Brien signed a Secured Promissory Note for $1.23M, making themselves personally liable as borrowers. They also signed a Pledge & Security Agreement through which they pledged their equity interests in Meade Transportation, Inc. (MTI) and Virginia Freight Holdings, LLC (VFH). The Note had a 30% interest rate and matured after 90-day. Their failure to repay caused a default in November 2023, which activated the 35% default interest rate.

As of October 1, 2025, approximately $2.5M remains due, and default interest continues to accrue at more than $1,100 each day. Although repeated demands have been made, they have neither paid nor proposed an acceptable repayment plan. Instead, they have tried to introduce “updated loan agreements” that would diminish my secured position and eliminate their personal liability.

My requested scope is straightforward:

Draft and issue, on your letterhead, a formal demand letter to Edwin Mason and John O’Brien that references their obligations under the Note and Security Agreement.

Mail the letter through U.S. Certified Mail so there is a formal delivery record.

Email Edwin and John afterward, attach the demand letter, advise them that it was sent by certified mail, and copy me.

For convenience, I have attached:

A chronology and balance-calculation summary

A draft demand letter for you to revise as appropriate

The Secured Promissory Note

The Pledge & Security Agreement

I would like this finished within the next week. Because most of the drafting has already been completed, I would prefer a reasonable flat fee. My main objective is to have the demand formally issued on your letterhead to create the record.

Please advise when you are available to speak and discuss the flat fee.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I appreciate the thorough background; it was very useful. In my experience, collection remains extremely difficult even when the documentation is strong (a note, guaranties, and pledged equity): debtors delay, transfer assets, banks are difficult to penetrate, and liens seldom produce cash. I do not perform forensic work or asset tracing. What I can provide is legal recourse from New York, principally a forceful demand that preserves the record. VA fraud complaints are an option we could attempt, although they are seldom productive, and the Note’s VA arbitration provision restricts remedies pursued outside Virginia. For a flat fee, I can draft the demand letter and handle certified mailing plus email, and I’m free to discuss it Sunday.
What would you charge to prepare the demand letter and handle certified mailing + email?

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_002],

I can handle this matter for a flat fee of $750. That fee would cover only the following:
• Reviewing the Note and Pledge/Security Agreement to understand the context,
• Preparing the formal demand letter,
• Mailing it by certified mail with proof of service, and
• Emailing a PDF copy.

The price also covers a few reasonable rounds of revisions needed to complete the draft. It excludes litigation, asset tracing, and any continuing correspondence beyond the letter itself.

Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Would you be willing to handle it for $500?

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_002],

I’m able to do the work for a flat fee of $625. The previously described scope and inclusions would stay unchanged, and I would additionally provide one follow-up email or letter if needed. Everything could be finalized by Sunday.

Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]—I’m unable to exceed $500. We can proceed if you can accept that amount, but I need your answer today. If not, I’ll need to pursue another option.

Mr. Ali, thank you for following up. I fully understand the limits of your budget, but regrettably I’m unable to accept $500 because it is somewhat below what I can charge for this kind of work.

I nevertheless appreciate being considered and remain available if you have general questions or would like guidance while proceeding. Best wishes with the project! Best, [FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001] —

I’m prepared to move ahead at $625 provided that the following is included:

Send two certified USPS letters to the two addresses I provide, and when they are mailed, send one related confirmation email to the two parties involved.

Manage as many as three email exchanges after the other party responds. I’ll prepare the replies, and you can transmit them for me.

Finish everything by Monday.

Please confirm whether that arrangement works.

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Thank you for defining the scope so clearly. I’m glad to proceed for $625 under the terms you outlined: sending the two certified USPS letters, issuing the email confirmations, and managing up to three follow-up email exchanges.

Your proposed schedule is workable. I likely won’t require the entire business day Monday, though I’d prefer to retain it as a modest buffer in case mailing or responses encounter minor delays.

If you agree, please confirm so I can begin.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Yes, let's move forward.
Please let me know once the contract is active. Thank you.
Paid and started

After our recent discussion, I examined the executed agreements. Stratagem Global Corporation is the signatory to both the Note and Security Agreement; Mason and O’Brien signed solely in their capacities as officers and did not sign personally.

Even so, I recommend leaving the demand letter unchanged. Continuing to address them individually preserves leverage and avoids alerting them to the issue. Should they later dispute personal liability, we could still advance fraud or alter-ego theories based on their actions.

Also, I located your email in my spam folder—thank you for directing me there!

Best,

Hello!

The records show that one package was delivered and the second was returned to me. The returned item arrived this morning, which is why my reply was delayed.

As part of my additional inquiry yesterday, I spoke with the delivery service and asked them to check every suite number in the building. They reported, however, that they could not locate any person or organization under that name. Consequently, I will mail another copy dated today to the official corporate address.

There has also been no reply to my earlier email. After the replacement mailing is sent and received at the company’s formal address, it will count as official delivery for all intents and purposes. At that stage, we can evaluate your available options.
Okay, excellent—thank you for updating me. Please notify me when they receive it at the new address, and then we can discuss strategy for the next step.

What time this morning can we send the email to the borrowers?

Hello! Although today was our original target for sending it, I believe the more prudent course may be to hold off until the original demand letter arrives at the corporate registered office. There seem to be some unexpected delays, which creates concern that avoidance tactics may be involved, much like what happened when we sent the first demand letter; this is quite unusual. Even so, we need to demonstrate that we provided ample time for receipt before taking the next step. If anything, these apparent avoidance tactics further support the argument for fraudulent and unlawful conduct.

With that in mind, I recommend waiting until Monday. By then, we can properly allege receipt of the initial demand letter and proceed from a stronger position. The final decision is, of course, yours.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Because we still have not received any acknowledgment from any of the addresses, even after the second demand letter, we are now left with four practical options:

- File a UCC-1 lien to formally protect your position and place the debt against the company’s pledged assets on the public record.
- Submit a fraud complaint to the FBI or the local District Attorney based on the continued evasion and possible misrepresentation of collateral.
- Engage a licensed research or skip-trace service to verify the principals’ current locations and locate any assets that can be reached.
- Commence a civil lawsuit \(either in D.C. or Virginia\) to secure a judgment and pursue enforcement through receivership or asset seizure.

Separately, I have completed both the original demand and an additional escalation letter that went beyond the original scope of our agreement. I also mailed a letter directly to the corporate address, which was outside the original scope as well. Therefore, if you are comfortable with it, I would like to send the invoice and the approximately \$70 in out-of-pocket expenses directly through Zelle or Venmo, then close the Upwork contract for payment so this stage can be finalized cleanly.

After that is resolved, we can proceed with whichever enforcement option you select.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
[FREELANCER_NAME_001] — thank you for the email. Didn’t I already pay you on upwork?
You did, but they hold the funds in escrow and release them once the project is complete. I wanted to confirm with you that the agreement could be closed.
That’s fine; you can close it.

Thank you! I’ll upload the incidentals for the mailing costs later, and once you determine how you want to proceed, I’ll be glad to help in any way I can. For any upcoming milestones or follow-up enforcement work, we can open a new contract.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
